summary: A horizontal slider: dragging or tapping the track sets its variable between min and max (the thumb jumps under the finger and follows it); it can show the value at its end, and onRelease runs actions with the released level (a host action sends it to the app). A screen reader hears the label and the current value.

value.doc: The value, kept in min..max. Bind a document variable ("@volume") to preset it and read it after the slider; omitted, the slider keeps its own. A drag writes the slider's OWN variable ("@volume" read after the slider is the live value); the bound variable itself (a resources variable, exported or not) is written only on release, and only when onRelease is given. To hand the level to the app, bind it and send it from onRelease: {"onRelease": {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "setVolume", "value": "@volume", "valueType": "float"}}

min.doc: Value at the left end of the track

max.doc: Value at the right end of the track

step.doc: Snap the value to multiples of this from min (0.25 for quarter hours, 5 for 5 % steps): the drag, the printed value and the release all snap. Omitted: continuous

label.doc: Accessibility label (the slider draws no title): put the visible name next to it and pass the same words

stateText.doc: What a screen reader hears as the value, when the raw number is not it: a text object over the live value read after the slider ("16:30" for 16.5 hours). Omitted: the value with `decimals` digits

showValue.doc: Print the value at the right end (the track gets 48 dp shorter)

decimals.doc: Digits after the point in the printed value

onRelease.doc: Actions run when the finger lifts after a drag or a tap (onTouchUp on the track). Before them the slider writes the released level into the bound variable, so an action that reads it gets the new value: {"type": "hostNamedAction", "name": "setVolume", "value": "@volume", "valueType": "float"} sends it to the app (valueType is a json2rc extension: the Java parser writes only a literal value), and an exported variable is updated too. Name the variable you bound to `value`, not "@value" (a param name, not substituted inside actions); an unbound slider's level cannot be named. Omitted: nothing runs on release and the bytes are unchanged

pitfalls: The drag is a touchExpression in absolute mode (touchMode 6) named after the bound variable: from the slider on, "@volume" is the touch value (it starts at the variable's own value and keeps where the finger left it). LIVE values derived from it (a preview, a time, a status) must be computed AFTER the slider in the tree: a text or canvas expression placed after it, or a tree `variable` command after it. The document's own resources.variables and computed resources.colors that read the bound name are moved there automatically by the expander (right after the slider), unless something reads them before the slider: then they update only on release (with onRelease), and expand_components warns

onRelease: the canvas carries an empty onTouchDown (without it Java never registers the canvas, so a drag runs no onTouchUp at all) and one onTouchUp list, in order (Java runs separate onTouchUp modifiers last first). The list recomputes the level from where the finger lifted into the bound variable, because modifiers come BEFORE the touchExpression and "@volume" there still names the bound (resources) variable; then it runs the caller's actions, which read it. A plain tap ends the same way. About 120 B per call with one host action
touchX() is in document coordinates, so the slider measures where it sits (componentValue POS_ROOT_X into a local) and subtracts it: it works anywhere in the layout, scrolled or padded

Inside a scrolling container, onRelease also fires for the last child wherever the finger lifts, and the dragged slider's own may not fire: the reference player does this, so a device does too. There, tell the app from the exported value instead of onRelease, or keep the slider outside the scroll. A plain Slider without onRelease is safe in a scroll
step snaps the value (round to multiples of step from min) in the drag and on release; without it the value is continuous (the notch stop modes need touchSpec, which the Java parser ignores, U8)
It fills the width it is given (fillMaxWidth) and is 40 dp tall: in a row, give it a weight or a box with a width
No easing on the value: the thumb follows the finger frame for frame (an animated value would trail it). In mono it looks the same, a thin grey track, a thicker white active part and a smaller thumb

Accessibility: a transparent box over the track carries the label and the value as its state (textFromFloat of the live value: `decimals` digits, at least 2 when max - min is under 1.5, so 0..1 reads 0.7, not 0; stateText replaces it, e.g. a time "16:30"). It comes after the canvas because only from the touchExpression on does the name read the dragged value; it takes no touch, so the drag still works. No role (the JSON semantics has no role key), and no adjust actions: a screen reader announces the value but cannot step it. About 85 B per call
A slider does not follow the app after a drag: the touch value wins from the first drag on. For a position the app keeps writing (a seek bar) use SeekBar
